text.what: Philadelphia sports-radio morning host, born 13 March 1951, whose WIP show founded Wing Bowl in 1993 and ran it for twenty-six years. A newspaperman first: Providence Journal from 1977, Philadelphia Inquirer sports from 1983, a Pulitzer finalist for covering the 1986 Eagles and Buddy Ryan.
text.story:
Cataldi joined WIP part-time in 1988 and took the morning show in 1993. The same year the show put on the first Wing Bowl — a wing-eating contest in a hotel lobby, two contestants, about 150 people watching, held on the Friday before a Super Bowl the Eagles were not in.

It grew into a 20,000-seat event at the Wells Fargo Center with a commissioner, a hall of fame, a women's bracket called the Wingettes, and a qualifying system of on-air eating stunts. Cataldi worked it as a promoter works a fight: going into 2008 he billed Wing Bowl XVI as the greatest ever, with Bill "El Wingador" Simmons coming out of retirement against Joey Chestnut. The 200-wing mark fell that day.

WIP cancelled it on 30 October 2018, after the Eagles won Super Bowl LII. Program director Spike Eskin gave the reason: "When Wing Bowl started ... a large part of it was the lead-up to the Super Bowl never involved the Eagles. We just wanted to get to the promised land."

Cataldi retired from the morning show on 17 February 2023 and signed off: "I mocked every athlete who said this when they retire, and I'm going to close by saying it myself — it's time for me to go, Philadelphia. I need to spend more time with my family. Thank you all for an amazing run. Goodbye." He wrote a memoir, Loud.
text.today: Wing Bowl returned on 7 February 2026 at the Plaza Hotel & Casino in Las Vegas with twenty competitors, and a documentary, No One Died: The Wing Bowl Story, was released on 15 August 2026. Sources read on 16 September 2026 record Cataldi as living.
